summary.text: A 69-year-old woman with seropositive myasthenia gravis on monthly IVIG, prednisone and pyridostigmine, with hypertension, coronary artery disease with a prior LAD stent, COPD and Grave's ophthalmopathy on methimazole, was transferred from a long-term acute care facility with acute chest pain, palpitations, nausea and sweating, together with worsening double vision, slurred nasal speech, difficulty swallowing saliva and generalized weakness.

The initial ECG showed ST elevations with troponin elevation concerning for STEMI, and emergent catheterization found no new coronary lesions with a patent prior stent. TTE confirmed mid ventricular variant Takotsubo stress cardiomyopathy with an ejection fraction of 25%. TSH was elevated with elevated thyroid autoantibodies, and neurology was consulted for myasthenia crisis management.

She was managed conservatively with five cycles of PLEX, with resolution of symptoms, ECG findings and troponemia, and was discharged back to the LTAC. Repeat TTE four weeks from admission showed complete resolution of left ventricular dysfunction, and prednisone and monthly IVIG were continued.

One year later she had a similar episode with ophthalmoparesis, generalized weakness, chest pain, troponemia and deep T wave inversions, and TTE showed mid and apical akinesia with an ejection fraction of 30%. She was diagnosed with recurrent Takotsubo stress cardiomyopathy secondary to myasthenia crisis, treated with five cycles of PLEX with resolution, and discharged to a rehabilitation facility; repeat TTE three weeks later showed normalized LV function with an ejection fraction of 60%.
